summary: A documentation release. The three READMEs are rebuilt around the agent skills the repository ships, so a reader can see that installing a skill is a first-class way to drive the project rather than a footnote.

highlights.title: The skills are the front door
highlights.body: Quick start now installs the skills first and the server second. The skills get their own section with the install command, a decision diagram and a table grouping them the way `skills.sh.json` does (CLI, MCP Tools, Workflows). The repository-layout block lists `skills/` and `skills.sh.json`.

highlights.title: The configuration table is complete
highlights.body: Ten `NOVELAI_*` defaults were missing: the default model, width, height, steps, scale and sampler, the upscale model, the timeout and both base URLs. The JSON form of the three routing-header lists is given below the table, since those variables must be JSON.

highlights.title: The three languages cannot drift apart
highlights.body: All three READMEs carry the same 39 headings, and `pnpm readme:check` fails if a code block, a table identifier or a configuration default stops matching. The Mermaid diagram and every code block are byte-identical across languages.

sections.title: 📝 Documentation
items: `README.md`, `.github/docs/README-zh.md` and `.github/docs/README-ja.md` rebuilt around the agent skills, with the same 39 headings in each language.
Quick start reordered: install the skills, then install the server from source, then from PyPI.
New Agent skills section: install command, decision diagram and a table grouped by CLI / MCP Tools / Workflows.
Configuration table completed with ten `NOVELAI_*` defaults, read from a running interpreter rather than recalled.

upgrade_notes: No runtime behaviour changes. The package contents are identical to 0.6.0; only the documentation changed. The one intentional behaviour change from 0.6.0 still applies: `director_tool`'s `emotion` and `emotion_level` require the `X-MCP-Insiders` opt-in.
